speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what are the crime statistics for the top 10 scams in Singapore for the past five years; and (b) what are the current resources in the Singapore Police Force that are dedicated to (i) solving online and phone scams as compared to the past five years and (ii) detecting and preventing online and phone scams.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In the past five years, the top scam types include e-commerce scams, loan scams, Internet love scams and credit-for-sex scams.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Member asked about Police resources dedicated to online and phone scams.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Since 2016, cybercrime investigation, digital forensics training, liaison and policy matters have been integrated under a single Cybercrime Command.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This has allowed the Singapore Police Force to achieve better coordination among the different units involved in cybercrime.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: All frontline Police officers and investigation officers have been trained in basic cybercrime investigations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In addition, officers with the aptitude for cybercrime investigations and digital forensics are given specialised training.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Third, better use of technology to help solve crimes, such as digital forensics, malware analysis and video analytics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police set up the Transnational Commercial Crime Task Force (TCTF) in October 2017 to tackle transnational online and phone scams.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police also set up an E-Commerce Fraud Enforcement and Coordination Team (E-FECT) in November 2018.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To prevent scams, the Police have been working very closely with stakeholders, such as convenience stores, remittance agencies and banks, to raise their awareness and develop suitable prevention measures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In the online space, too, the Police have engaged major online shopping platforms to implement measures to safeguard consumers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: An example is Police’s partnership with Carousell to remove suspicious advertisements on their platform, introduce a secure payment system, and feature scam advisories.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police have also been working with the National Crime Prevention Council (NCPC) to step up public education on online and phone scams.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police have also set up an Anti-Scam Helpline (1800-722-6688) and the www.scamalert.sg website.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Members of the public are encouraged to visit the website to learn about the various types of scams and take steps to avoid becoming a victim.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: It is quite clear that the cybercrime trend has been going up.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: The Police not only need physical strength to catch the culprit, they also need cyber strength and cyber technology to help them better detect and solve the cybercrimes.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: First, are there dedicated resources at the front line in the Police Division, in the investigation team?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Are there people dedicated to solve and take care of cybercrime and phone scams?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: We know that the turnover for counter staff is high.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: So, what are the efforts to continue to educate them, especially new staff?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Member asked about training of frontline officers.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: In my reply, I mentioned about the training of frontline Police officers and investigation officers, that they have been trained in basic cybercrime investigations.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: In particular, officers with an aptitude for cybercrime investigations and digital forensics are given digitalised training.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: In addition, we have various specialised units that tackle cybercrime.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: On the issue of banks and the other stores and the turnover of staff, I think that is a valid point.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I do not have the exact numbers in terms of the number of staff that have been trained.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This goes to show that ongoing training and continuous outreach are very, very important, given the turnover of staff.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: But it is something that we have to keep doing and do better.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The key thing is the role of individuals to take precautionary measures to understand that some things are just too good to be true and, so, to take prevention measures at their end.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Other than that, the other measures are something that we will keep doing and trying.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: But the individual is the best defence against cybercrimes.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: One more question: is there a dedicated unit at the Division to investigate cybercrime, or it is just part of their general duties?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: If there is no dedicated unit in the Division, will the Police consider setting one up in the near future?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I think the thrust of the question is whether there is capability on the ground to address cybercrime issues.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: So, it is a concerted, comprehensive effort, a multi-prong approach towards tackling this issue.
